---
title: "juphyter"
subtitle: "A Jupyter and Quarto kernel for PHP"
jupyter: php
---

juphyter runs PHP code in notebooks and in Quarto documents.

A notebook is a file of cells. Each cell holds a few lines of code, and its
output appears directly beneath it: text, a table, or a chart. The program
that runs the cells is called a kernel, and it keeps one PHP session open, so a
variable set in one cell is available in the next.
[JupyterLab](https://jupyter.org/) is the usual application for editing and
running notebooks. [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) renders a Markdown document
with code cells into HTML, PDF, or Word, running each cell and placing its
output in the document.

juphyter is that kernel for PHP. After `juphyter install`, JupyterLab lists PHP
in its launcher, and Quarto runs the `{php}` cells of any `.qmd` that names
the kernel in its front matter. It is meant for statistical and exploratory
work with the phpstats packages: load data, try a pipeline, look at the
table or the plot it produces, and change the code until the result is right.

## What a cell shows

The value of a cell's last expression is its output. A
[phibble](https://phibble.phpstats.org) data frame appears as an HTML table
with its dimensions and column types, and a
[phiz](https://phiz.phpstats.org) plot appears as a chart. Other values appear
as a compact dump.

```{php}
#| echo: false
use function Phplyr\{phplyr, group_by, summarize, arrange, desc, n, mean};
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}

## PHP 8.5+

```{php}
$mpg = \Phibble\DataFrame::fromRows(\Phiz\Datasets::mpg());

$mpg |>
    group_by('class') |>
    summarize(models: n(), hwy: mean('hwy')) |>
    arrange(desc('hwy'));
```

## PHP 8.3–8.4

```{php}
$mpg = \Phibble\DataFrame::fromRows(\Phiz\Datasets::mpg());

phplyr($mpg)
    ->groupBy('class')
    ->summarize(models: n(), hwy: mean('hwy'))
    ->arrange(desc('hwy'))
    ->get();
```

:::

```{php}
#| fig-cap: "Highway mileage against engine displacement."
\Phiz\Plot::of(\Phiz\Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(opacity: 0.7)
    ->smooth(method: 'lm')
    ->labs(x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg', color: 'Drive');
```

## What the kernel provides

- State across cells, including `use` imports and declared functions and
  classes.
- Tracebacks that name the cell and the line, instead of `eval()'d code`.
- HTML tables for phibble data frames and charts for phiz plots, plus
  `toHtml()` and `toMimeBundle()` hooks for any other class.
- `Juphyter\display()`, which shows a value part way through a cell.
- Completion of variables, functions, classes, and members.
- Interrupting a running cell with the stop button, when PHP has the `pcntl`
  extension.
- Loading the nearest `vendor/autoload.php` above the notebook, so a notebook
  inside a Composer project can use that project's classes and packages.

juphyter requires none of the phpstats packages. It runs plain PHP, and it
formats a phibble data frame or a phiz plot when those packages are
installed.

## How it works

The kernel has two processes. A small Python program built on
[ipykernel](https://github.com/ipython/ipykernel) handles the Jupyter
protocol, and a PHP process runs the cells. They talk over a Unix socket. This
is why an install needs a Python with ipykernel as well as PHP, and why the
kernel runs on macOS and Linux only.

[Installation](install.qmd) covers the requirements and the install
commands, and [Getting started](get-started.qmd) walks through a first
notebook.
